findings.Quote: The fight was brief and unkind.
findings.Note: Vague abstraction stands in for description; 'unkind' tells the reader how to feel about a fight we don't see.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with one concrete physical beat of the fight.

findings.Quote: A thing to use or a thing to die on.
findings.Note: Aphoristic phrasing that leans toward a stock tough-narrator maxim rather than concrete observation.
findings.Fix: Cut or ground it in specific tactical detail: "Loose rail, thirty degrees of swing — leverage or a liability, depending who reached it first."

findings.Quote: his position exactly where she'd have put herself in his place
findings.Note: Tells us the tactical read via summary rather than letting the listed details (stair access, cover, wind) speak for themselves — redundant framing.
findings.Fix: Cut the lead-in clause and let the list stand alone: "Clear line to the stair access, cover behind the shelter angle, wind at his back."

findings.Quote: It cost her nothing. It was the right call, made by the person best placed to make it.
findings.Note: Flat aphoristic summary that states the beat's conclusion instead of dramatizing Rook's assessment; reads as authorial commentary.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete beat of Rook's attention moving on: "Rook filed it and moved past — column held, line clear, nothing here needed her."

findings.Quote: Not faster than her — no one who'd been operating at his level for four hours was faster than anyone — but adapted
findings.Note: the aphoristic aside about operating for four hours reads as a generalized truism inserted for flavor rather than earned observation, and it's a slightly clunky construction to parse mid-action
findings.Fix: Not faster than her — four hours in, fatigue was already eating his margin — but adapted

findings.Quote: reading her weight shifts the way you read them when you've done this enough that the reading is below thought
findings.Note: 'below thought' as a description of expert instinct is a familiar formulation for trained-reflex competence
findings.Fix: reading her weight shifts on reflex, no conscious step between sensing and answering

findings.Quote: It's a cold way to be right.
findings.Note: reads as a scripted, quotable line-of-dialogue aphorism rather than something a cornered professional would actually say in the moment
findings.Fix: Cold logic. He didn't argue it.

findings.Quote: kept his arms at his sides
findings.Note: presented as the one thing he did right, but the detail is generic enough (arms-at-sides is standard fall-safety advice) that it doesn't land as a specific, earned observation of his skill
findings.Fix: kept his arms tucked, chin down, taking the water like he'd rehearsed it

findings.Quote: sighting through the viewport glass at exactly the angle she'd have asked for if she could have asked
findings.Note: convoluted hypothetical phrasing that tells rather than shows precision, weakens the visual
findings.Fix: sighting through the viewport glass at the exact angle she needed

findings.Quote: He was grinning — she could tell from twenty meters in the dark
findings.Note: strains credulity/mechanics — grinning discernible at twenty meters in rain and dark undercuts the otherwise grounded visual detail
findings.Fix: cut the distance/dark qualifier or replace with something she could plausibly perceive, like his posture or a shout

findings.Quote: The node did it without drama, because it was built to transmit and this was what it did.
findings.Note: tautological filler aphorism that states the obvious rather than adding meaning
findings.Fix: cut the sentence or replace with a concrete detail of the transmission's effect

findings.Quote: Pulling out was correct. Rook would have done the same.
findings.Note: Reads as an authorial aphorism/justification inserted to reassure the reader rather than dramatized judgment from a POV character; flat assertion of correctness twice in two sentences.
findings.Fix: Cut the second sentence or attribute the judgment to a specific character's thought.

findings.Quote: the rule was behind her
findings.Note: Vague abstraction — unclear what physical or narrative referent 'the rule' has in this sentence; reads as filler tension-language rather than concrete stakes.
findings.Fix: Name the rule or replace with a concrete detail about what she's leaving behind.

findings.Quote: The pilot was good, and she was better
findings.Fix: Cut the comparative claim; let the action of getting through the hatch demonstrate skill without stating it.

findings.Quote: The altitude question had been settled by her presence in the cockpit.
findings.Fix: Cut this explanatory line; the scene already shows it.

findings.Quote: three becoming two becoming one becoming silence
findings.Note: reaches for lyrical patterning on a mechanical detail (agents disconnecting); the repetition strains for gravity it hasn't earned
findings.Fix: Vox was in the maintenance VTOL, watching the agent channels close one by one.

findings.Quote: She hadn't been present for any of it, and she'd been essential to all of it.
findings.Note: aphoristic paradox-statement that restates the previous paragraph's point rather than adding information
findings.Fix: cut the sentence or replace with a concrete detail about what her crawlers did

findings.Quote: The questions would take a while to arrive.
findings.Note: vague portentous stinger that doesn't specify anything concrete, functioning as a filler-wit closer
findings.Fix: specify a beat, e.g. 'Rook didn't plan to be there when they did.'

findings.Quote: something quieter, aimed at the people who had carried her numbers home
findings.Fix: either name the emotion or cut the negation setup ('not gratitude...') which promises precision it doesn't deliver

findings.Quote: her hands did the count out of habit and came up five
findings.Fix: clarify mechanics — hands don't count, have her fingers move or just state she counted

findings.Quote: It was the one ritual she still let herself keep — hands doing a small honest thing while the rest of her caught up.
findings.Note: Tells the reader the emotional function of the counting rather than trusting the preceding demonstration; slightly purple aphorism-adjacent phrasing.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory sentence or replace with a concrete physical beat that shows rather than states the ritual's purpose.

findings.Quote: Ohara had wanted one specific lock broken, and it was broken, and the door it had been on now stood open to everyone.
findings.Note: Mixed metaphor stacking (lock/door/broken) restates the same idea three ways without adding information.
findings.Fix: Trim to one image: 'Ohara had wanted the lock broken. It was broken, and the door stood open to everyone now.'

findings.Quote: spent four years and her whole career being willing to be right about it
findings.Note: Vague aphoristic close-out that tells us she took a risk without showing the stakes or cost concretely.
findings.Fix: Specify what the career cost was, or cut the abstraction.

findings.Quote: He was the kind of asset that survived because he was built to.
findings.Note: Stock tautological tough-guy phrasing ('built to survive') that reads as filler characterization rather than specific insight.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete detail about his tradecraft or history that shows why he survives.

findings.Quote: It's a cold way to be right
findings.Note: Aphorism doing double duty as both dialogue and thematic summary; feels inserted for resonance rather than earned in-scene.
findings.Fix: Ground the line in the specific stakes of that conversation rather than leaving it as a floating maxim.

findings.Quote: the courtesy of the work and not its coldness
findings.Note: Abstract distinction stated rather than demonstrated; reads as authorial explanation of feeling rather than dramatized detail.
findings.Fix: Show one small habitual action that embodies 'courtesy' instead of naming the abstraction.

findings.Quote: hoping the next one would line up while they still owed each other nothing but the wanting to
findings.Note: Convoluted phrasing obscures rather than clarifies the emotional beat; syntax undercuts the intended plainness.
findings.Fix: Simplify: 'hoping the next job would line up before they owed each other anything more than the wanting to.'

findings.Quote: Three channels instead of six now, down from the four she'd carried into the flat.
findings.Note: Numbers are internally confusing — 'six' and 'four' both referenced as prior states without clarifying which is accurate, reads as a continuity slip within the sentence itself.
findings.Fix: Clarify the sequence explicitly: 'Six before Rotterdam, four into the flat, three now.'

findings.Quote: Rook hadn't done any of that before.
findings.Note: Flat telling-summary tacked onto the end, naming the significance instead of trusting the preceding details to carry it.
findings.Fix: Cut the line and let the prior images stand alone, or fold the realization into action/thought earlier.

findings.Quote: It was honest that way.
findings.Note: Slides toward pseudo-profound aphorism explaining the emotional math rather than trusting the preceding image.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; let the unbalanced count speak for itself.
